title: Sharp Joint Regions of Arm-Specific Outcome Distributions in Saturated Selector Stars
banked_reason: DuarteEtAl2024 already provides finite full-data response representations and sharp optimization for arbitrary discrete SCMs, while the remaining displayed simplexes and support formula are standard missing-mass/convex-geometry reductions; the literal selector encoding does not create a field-level new result.

tldr: For the finite saturated selector star whose literal labelled projection reaches SS-ID Algorithm 2 line 3, the project proves an exact forward-and-inverse response theorem and uses it to identify the full joint region of arm-specific natural-outcome distributions as translated covariate-stratum simplexes. Every region point, every scalar corner, and every finite-score support optimizer is realized by one finite graph-compatible SCM that preserves all factual selector labels and cells. Closed scalar endpoints, a same-arm-aware support formula, a compact witness bound, and standard bounded-score outer coverage follow. The contribution is an incremental selector-specific completion of classical missing-outcome geometry, not a new graphical criterion or a general response-optimization theorem.
gap: SS-ID certifies nonidentification at Algorithm 2 line 3 but stops before describing the compatible causal region. Classical missing-data work supplies the simplex geometry, while generic discrete-SCM optimization supplies finite response representations, but neither verifies the literal selector-labelled inverse realization at this failure branch.
fill: The forward-and-inverse response theorem establishes exact observable compatibility, the joint completion theorem gives the translated-simplex region, and the support and inference corollaries turn that region into finite certificates and reportable bounds.
